The method is carried out using a sawing machine that includes a machine bench, a pair of clamping jaws, and an upper saw. The upper saw is movable in a cutting plane in order to cut a workpiece positioned on the bench.

At the beginning of the method, the workpiece is placed on the machine bench and is gripped by the clamping jaws. At this stage, the clamping jaws are located in an initial position. The workpiece is therefore first secured in this initial position so that it can be moved in a controlled manner by the machine.

An offset value is then entered into the controller of the sawing machine. This offset value represents the distance between the front end of the workpiece and a defined zero position of the machine. By using this value, the controller can determine how far the workpiece must be displaced in order to bring its front end into the zero position.

After the offset value has been entered, the clamping jaws move the workpiece toward the zero position. Once the workpiece has reached this zero position, the clamping jaws release the workpiece. The clamping jaws then return to their initial position without moving the workpiece.

When the clamping jaws have returned to the initial position, they clamp the workpiece again. The workpiece is now located at the zero position and is securely held by the clamping jaws. From this zero position, the clamping jaws move the workpiece into the intended cutting position, in which the desired cut is aligned with the cutting plane of the upper saw. The upper saw can then be moved in the cutting plane to perform the cutting operation.

A metal sawing method is carried out using a sawing machine equipped with a machine controller, a support bench, clamping jaws, and an upper saw arranged to cut a workpiece in a defined cutting plane. The workpiece is first placed on the bench and held by the clamping jaws. An operator or automated system enters into the machine controller an offset value that represents the desired distance between a reference or zero position and the final cutting position of the workpiece.

After the offset has been entered, the controller moves the workpiece toward the predetermined zero position. Once the workpiece reaches this zero position, the clamping jaws are released or reset so that the workpiece can be accurately referenced. The jaws are then re-engaged to clamp the workpiece securely in the corrected position. From this accurately established zero position, the controller advances the workpiece by the programmed offset distance until the workpiece reaches the intended cutting position beneath the upper saw.

When the workpiece is positioned in the cutting plane, the upper saw is actuated to perform the sawing operation. Because the workpiece has first been aligned with a known zero position and then moved by a controlled offset, the cutting location can be set with a high degree of accuracy. Releasing, resetting, and re-clamping the jaws before the final advance reduces positioning errors that may arise from initial placement, backlash, slippage, or tolerance variations in the feed mechanism.

This method therefore provides a reliable and repeatable way to align metal workpieces before cutting. It improves cutting precision, ensures consistent positioning from one workpiece to the next, and is particularly useful where accurate lengths or repeated cuts are required in metal sawing operations.

**The Power of “The”**

The word **“the”** may be small, but it is one of the most important words in the English language. It is called the **definite article**, and it is used to refer to a specific person, place, thing, or idea. For example, when we say **“the book,”** we are not talking about any book—we mean a particular book that the speaker and listener understand.

“The” helps make communication clearer. It points to something known, unique, or already mentioned. We say **“the sun”** because there is only one sun in our sky. We say **“the teacher”** when both people know which teacher is being discussed.

Although it is a very common word, “the” plays a powerful role in shaping meaning. Without it, sentences can sound unclear or incomplete. This simple word helps organize language and guide the reader or listener toward the exact meaning intended.

In short, **“the”** is a tiny word with a big purpose. It adds precision, clarity, and structure to English communication.

## Invention Summary

The invention relates to a CNC metal sawing machine and an automatic workpiece referencing method for accurately positioning a workpiece prior to cutting. The machine includes a saw unit defining a cutting plane zero position, a workpiece feed system, movable clamping jaws for holding and advancing the workpiece, and a CNC controller configured to execute a referencing routine based on an operator-entered offset value.

In operation, the operator enters an offset value corresponding to the distance between a known reference position of the workpiece or clamping system and the front end side of the workpiece. The CNC controller then drives the clamping jaws to move the workpiece such that the front end side of the workpiece is positioned at the cutting plane zero position. This establishes a precise reference between the actual workpiece end and the saw cutting plane without requiring manual alignment or separate measurement at the saw blade.

After the front end side has been referenced to the cutting plane zero position, the clamping jaws are returned to their initial position. The CNC controller then advances the workpiece from the referenced position by the programmed cutting length or other intended feed distance so that the workpiece is accurately located for the desired cut.

By using the entered offset value to automatically reference the workpiece end relative to the cutting plane, the invention reduces setup time, improves positioning accuracy, minimizes operator intervention, and enables repeatable CNC-controlled cutting operations, particularly in applications involving bar stock, profiles, tubes, or other elongated metal workpieces.
